title: Launch brief (lite) and role-bound changelog guardrails
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a compact, role-bound changelog process and a "lite" launch brief template that enables rapid releases (hotfixes, minor feature drops) without sacrificing cross-team signoff, customer clarity, or compliance needs.
background: As Redwood expands Dedicated and Private deployments, small iterative releases have increased frequency. Existing release note playbooks are comprehensive but heavyweight for low-risk changes, causing latency in publishing and inconsistent customer messaging. We need a streamlined flow that scopes what must be full-reviewed vs what can follow a lightweight lane.
objectives: Define a 1-page 'Launch Brief (Lite)' template that captures impact, rollback plan, and SLO/customer notes
Create role-bound guardrails that specify who must review or can opt-out for low-risk releases
Automate notification and minimal signoff collection to enable same-day publish for qualifying changes
Provide clear mapping to full changelog process when risk or compliance requires escalation
success_metrics: Reduce median time from merge to customer-facing changelog publish for P2/P3 releases from 48h to <8h
Increase percent of qualifying releases using 'lite' flow to 60% within first quarter
Fewer post-release support tickets attributable to ambiguous release notes (target: -30% for lite flows)
stakeholders: Product Management: Ava Martinez (owner), Priya Rao
review_flow: Triage -> Lite-check rubric -> Auto-notify required reviewers -> 2-hour soft hold for objections -> Signoff recorded in ticket -> Publish
signoff_matrix: Eng lead: required for changes touching runtime or infra
Design: advisory for UX-affecting items, required only if UX changes are present
Security & Compliance: required if data, RBAC, KMS, or audit surface area changes
Support: advisory for customer-impacting messages, required for breaking changes
Legal: required only for changes that reference SLAs/pricing or contractual language
timeline: Week 1: Draft template and lite-risk rubric (PM + Eng + Security)
Week 2: Run pilot with 4 low-risk releases across hosted API and Dedicated
Week 3: Collect feedback, refine notification hooks and minimal signoff automation
Week 4: Roll out playbook and update Console 'Release notes' guide
deliverables: Launch Brief (Lite) template (1-page Markdown) with example entries
Lite-risk rubric (checkbox list) to decide eligibility
Signoff automation checklist (Slack + ticket flags) + sample automation recipe
Owner matrix and documentation page in Confluence
Pilot report with metrics and recommended guardrail tweaks
dependencies: Engineering: small webhook to flip 'lite' flag on Linear tickets (ENG-20488)
Console Docs: place to host public changelog fragments (DOCS-1102)
Support: training doc and canned response updates (SUP-331)
risks: Under-specified lite rubric leads to customer confusion or missed compliance reviews
Automation gaps could surface partial signoffs and leave gaps in audit trails
Teams may default to lite flow for borderline items, increasing downstream support load
open_questions: What minimum metadata must a lite brief include to be searchable in the release catalog?
Should we allow retrospective escalation from lite to full review after publish? If so, how are customers notified?
What is the SLA for reviewer response before auto-approval (2h vs 4h)?
